rituals.name: FOLD THE NEXT STEP
rituals.title: FOLD THE NEXT STEP
rituals.targetPattern: Unfinished task kept mentally active
rituals.target_pattern: Unfinished task kept mentally active
rituals.precise_subpattern: Unfinished task kept mentally active
rituals.vibeLine: Outsourced one open tab to stationery.
rituals.hook: Give the unfinished thing somewhere physical to live besides your head.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your mind will keep rehearsing the task after the next action is captured externally.
rituals.play: Write exactly one next physical action on a small piece of paper: “email Sam,” “open invoice,” “put form in bag.” Fold the paper and place it where you will see it later.
rituals.catch: Wait ten seconds and check whether the task feels equally necessary to rehearse.
rituals.reveal: A captured next step can reduce the brain’s need to keep an unfinished intention active.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes your mind repeats a task because it does not trust that the task has somewhere else to live.

rituals.vibeLine: Hard to sound like destiny at chipmunk speed.
rituals.hook: Your loop has been using prestige-drama pacing.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the thought feels equally authoritative at ridiculous double speed.
rituals.play: Replay the exact thought in your head at absurdly fast cartoon speed. No pausing for emotional emphasis. Run it through three times.
rituals.catch: Check if it becomes harder to treat each phrase like a solemn revelation.
rituals.reveal: Processing style changes emotional weight even when the words are identical.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can feel profound partly because you keep giving it dramatic pacing.

Replay the exact thought in your head at absurdly fast cartoon speed. No pausing for emotional emphasis. Run it through three times.
Guess whether the thought feels equally authoritative at ridiculous double speed.
Check if it becomes harder to treat each phrase like a solemn revelation. Processing style changes emotional weight even when the words are identical.

rituals.name: WRONG VOICE CASTING

rituals.targetPattern: Authority attached to internal voice
rituals.target_pattern: Authority attached to internal voice
rituals.precise_subpattern: Authority attached to internal voice
rituals.vibeLine: Your thought just lost its serious-actor contract.
rituals.hook: Your thought has been badly typecast as “serious narrator.”
rituals.predict: Guess which absurd voice makes the loop lose the most authority.
rituals.play: Hear the sentence in three voices: sleepy robot, game-show host, bored GPS. Use the exact words.
rituals.catch: Check if the message feels different when the speaker identity changes.
rituals.reveal: The brain confuses familiar delivery with credibility more than we notice.
rituals.mindBend: A thought does not become wiser because it uses your most convincing inner voice.

rituals.vibeLine: Your loop now has attendance records.
rituals.hook: Stop arguing with the thought.
rituals.predict: Guess how many times the same theme will return in thirty seconds.
rituals.play: For 30 sec, do nothing to stop the loop. Each time it returns, tap one finger. No analysis, just count entrances.
rituals.catch: Compare the count with your prediction and notice whether counting changes the rhythm.
rituals.reveal: Measuring a loop turns you from participant into observer for a moment.
rituals.mindBend: The moment you can count a thought, you are not completely inside it.

rituals.name: CLOSE ONE TAB
rituals.title: CLOSE ONE TAB
rituals.targetPattern: Multiple unfinished tasks creating mental load
rituals.target_pattern: Multiple unfinished tasks creating mental load
rituals.precise_subpattern: Multiple unfinished tasks creating mental load
rituals.vibeLine: We closed exactly one thing and refused to become a productivity influencer.
rituals.hook: Do not organise your whole life.
rituals.predict: Guess whether finishing one two-minute loose end changes the mental noise at all.
rituals.play: Name three open loops. Pick the smallest one that can be genuinely finished in under two minutes—send, file, throw away, book, put away, confirm. Finish only that one.
rituals.catch: Check if the other two feel even slightly less crowded after one closure.
rituals.reveal: Completion gives the brain a concrete signal that not every open loop is permanent.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to clear the whole desk to prove that tabs can close.

Name three open loops. Pick the smallest one that can be genuinely finished in under two minutes—send, file, throw away, book, put away, confirm. Finish only that one.
Guess whether finishing one two-minute loose end changes the mental noise at all.
Check if the other two feel even slightly less crowded after one closure. Completion gives the brain a concrete signal that not every open loop is permanent.
↻ CLOSE ONE TAB
unfiltered.fullVersion:

VIBE: UNFILTERED

You do not need to fix your life. Close one damn tab.

rituals.name: REVERSE THE MEMORY
rituals.title: REVERSE THE MEMORY
rituals.targetPattern: Memory replay following same causal path
rituals.target_pattern: Memory replay following same causal path
rituals.precise_subpattern: Memory replay following same causal path
rituals.vibeLine: Your memory hates driving backwards because the plot stops looking so inevitable.
rituals.hook: Your memory keeps taking the same road.
rituals.predict: Guess which detail becomes harder to connect when the story runs from end to beginning.
rituals.play: Start at the final moment of the memory. Step backward scene by scene until the beginning. Don’t explain causes—only move backward through observable moments.
rituals.catch: Catch where the usual “and therefore…” story becomes awkward to maintain.
rituals.reveal: Narrative order creates causal smoothness. Reverse order disrupts that automatic storyline.
rituals.mindBend: A memory feels inevitable partly because you always replay it in the same direction.

rituals.name: BOOKED FOR 7:13
rituals.title: BOOKED FOR 7:13
rituals.targetPattern: Belief worry must be solved immediately
rituals.target_pattern: Belief worry must be solved immediately
rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief worry must be solved immediately
rituals.vibeLine: Urgent thought downgraded to scheduled meeting.
rituals.hook: Give the worry an oddly specific appointment.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your brain will accept “later” more easily when later has an exact time.
rituals.play: Choose a real time later today, like 7:13 pm, for ten minutes of worry. Write it down. When the thought returns, Don’t argue—say “booked for 7:13.”
rituals.catch: Check if postponement feels different from suppression.
rituals.reveal: The brain may release an item more readily when it trusts there is a defined return point.
rituals.mindBend: Postponing a thought is not pretending it does not exist. It is refusing emergency status.

rituals.name: WHITE BEAR’S COUSIN
rituals.title: WHITE BEAR’S COUSIN
rituals.targetPattern: Rebound from trying not to think
rituals.target_pattern: Rebound from trying not to think
rituals.precise_subpattern: Rebound from trying not to think
rituals.vibeLine: The ban needed a security guard staring directly at the thought.
rituals.hook: For five seconds, absolutely do not think the thought.
rituals.predict: Guess whether forcefully banning it will make it appear less or more.
rituals.play: Set five seconds. Try hard not to think the target thought. The instant it appears, just notice that the ban itself kept checking for it.
rituals.catch: Catch the monitoring process asking, “Am I thinking it yet?”
rituals.reveal: Suppression requires searching for the thing you are trying to exclude.
rituals.mindBend: To check that a thought is gone, the brain has to keep looking for it.

rituals.target_pattern: Repetition mistaken for problem solving
rituals.precise_subpattern: Repetition mistaken for problem solving
rituals.vibeLine: Lots of thinking. Shockingly little new data.
rituals.hook: If this is problem solving, it should be producing something new.
rituals.predict: Guess how many genuinely new facts appeared in the last three loops.
rituals.play: Replay the last three rounds mentally. For each, name one new fact, decision or action that did not exist before. If there is none, mark it “replay.”
rituals.catch: Notice the difference between thinking longer and learning more.
rituals.reveal: Repetition can feel effortful without generating information.
rituals.mindBend: Mental effort is not the same thing as mental progress.

cheeky.predict: Guess how many genuinely new facts appeared in the last three loops.
cheeky.play: Replay the last three rounds mentally. For each, name one new fact, decision or action that did not exist before. If there is none, mark it “replay.”
cheeky.catch: Notice the difference between thinking longer and learning more.
cheeky.reveal: Repetition can feel effortful without generating information.
cheeky.mindBend: Mental effort is not the same thing as mental progress.
cheeky.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the memory/imagery pass brief and single-pass. Stop if repeating it makes the thought louder, more detailed or harder to leave. The result is a working perspective, not proof that the opposite story is true.
cheeky.targetPattern: Repetition mistaken for problem solving
cheeky.mechanismFingerprint: Audit recent rumination cycles for novel information/action output versus pure repetition.

rituals.name: PUT IT ON THE WALL
rituals.title: PUT IT ON THE WALL
rituals.targetPattern: Thought experienced as located inside self
rituals.target_pattern: Thought experienced as located inside self
rituals.precise_subpattern: Thought experienced as located inside self
rituals.vibeLine: Thought relocated. Rent remains unpaid.
rituals.hook: Your thought feels inside your head.
rituals.predict: Guess where in the room the thought would “sit” if it had to occupy a physical spot.
rituals.play: Point to a wall, chair or object and imagine the sentence printed there. Move your eyes to it, then away from it, then back.
rituals.catch: Check if the thought becomes something you can look toward rather than something you are inside.
rituals.reveal: Spatialising mental content can create a simple sense of distance without denying the content.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can be something you notice, not a room you are trapped inside.

rituals.name: STOP BEFORE THE LAST WORD
rituals.title: STOP BEFORE THE LAST WORD
rituals.targetPattern: Need to finish a mental sentence
rituals.target_pattern: Need to finish a mental sentence
rituals.precise_subpattern: Need to finish a mental sentence
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain is furious about one missing word. Adorable.
rituals.hook: Your brain hates an unfinished sentence.
rituals.predict: Guess how strong the urge will be to complete a familiar loop if you stop one word early.
rituals.play: Begin the repeating sentence and deliberately stop before the final word. Hold the blank for five seconds. Don’t fill it.
rituals.catch: Feel the pull to complete the phrase.
rituals.reveal: The urge to finish can be mistaken for the importance of the content itself.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes the loop wants completion, not truth.

rituals.name: SEARCH BAR TEST
rituals.title: SEARCH BAR TEST
rituals.targetPattern: Treating existential uncertainty like searchable information
rituals.target_pattern: Treating existential uncertainty like searchable information
rituals.precise_subpattern: Treating existential uncertainty like searchable information
rituals.vibeLine: Your loop put on reading glasses and called itself research.
rituals.hook: Would you type this question into a search bar expecting one factual answer?
rituals.predict: Guess whether the loop is actually asking for information or demanding impossible certainty.
rituals.play: Phrase the loop as a search query. Ask: “What observable answer could a search engine, expert or experiment return?” If none exists, rename it from “research” to “uncertainty.”
rituals.catch: Notice how many “why me / what if forever / how do I know for sure” questions have no finite lookup result.
rituals.reveal: Some loops persist because the mind keeps searching for an answer that the question cannot structurally provide.
rituals.mindBend: Not every question is a research task. Some are uncertainty wearing glasses.

cheeky.openingLine:
Same thought, different venue. Reviews may vary.

Your loop may have a favourite seat.
cheeky.ritualCard:
Your loop may have a favourite seat.
Without solving anything, stand up and move to a different chair, doorway, room corner or safe spot. Once there, say only the loop’s headline once.
Guess whether the thought changes texture if your body changes location by a few metres.
Check if the loop restarts automatically, weakens, changes pace, or feels oddly out of place. Repeated thinking can become linked to context cues as well as content.
↻ MOVE THE LOOP’S CHAIR

rituals.name: HUM THE SENTENCE

rituals.targetPattern: Meaning reinforced by ordinary speech rhythm
rituals.target_pattern: Meaning reinforced by ordinary speech rhythm
rituals.precise_subpattern: Meaning reinforced by ordinary speech rhythm
rituals.vibeLine: Lyrics removed. Authority oddly reduced.
rituals.hook: Your thought has lyrics.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the sentence keeps the same authority when the words disappear.
rituals.play: Take the rhythm of the looping sentence and hum it without words for five seconds. Say the sentence normally once.
rituals.catch: Notice the strange gap between the sound pattern and the meaning attached to it.
rituals.reveal: Language can feel inseparable from truth until its sound and meaning are pulled apart.
rituals.mindBend: A thought is partly meaning—and partly just a noise pattern your mouth can hum.

rituals.name: GUESS THE NEXT LINE
rituals.title: GUESS THE NEXT LINE
rituals.targetPattern: Repetition mistaken for discovery
rituals.target_pattern: Repetition mistaken for discovery
rituals.precise_subpattern: Repetition mistaken for discovery
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain is airing reruns and calling them breaking news.
rituals.hook: If you know the next line, this may be a rerun.
rituals.predict: Guess the exact next sentence your mind will produce.
rituals.play: Pause. Say or write your prediction. Let the loop continue for a few seconds and compare.
rituals.catch: If you predicted it, mark it RERUN rather than NEW INFORMATION.
rituals.reveal: Predictable thinking can still feel urgent because familiarity does not stop emotional activation.
rituals.mindBend: If you can write the next line before your brain says it, you are probably not discovering anything.

rituals.targetPattern: Dynamic replay keeping an event emotionally live
rituals.target_pattern: Dynamic replay keeping an event emotionally live
rituals.precise_subpattern: Dynamic replay keeping an event emotionally live
rituals.vibeLine: The memory lost its chase scene.
rituals.hook: Your memory keeps moving.
rituals.predict: Guess which single image represents the whole replay most strongly.
rituals.play: Stop the mental movie on one frame. Describe only the static visual details in that frame for 10 sec. No before, no after, no explanation.
rituals.catch: Notice what happens when the causal motion disappears.
rituals.reveal: Narrative movement helps memories keep generating consequences and meanings.
rituals.mindBend: A memory is easier to chase when it keeps running.

rituals.name: SEQUEL CAP
rituals.title: SEQUEL CAP
rituals.targetPattern: Each imagined problem spawning another
rituals.target_pattern: Each imagined problem spawning another
rituals.precise_subpattern: Each imagined problem spawning another
rituals.vibeLine: Your worry franchise has been capped at one sequel.
rituals.hook: Your worry chain keeps manufacturing sequels.
rituals.predict: Guess how many “and then…” links appear after the first concern.
rituals.play: State the first feared event. Allow exactly one “and then…” consequence. Stop before the second. Put every later consequence behind an imaginary locked door.
rituals.catch: Notice how much of the emotional load lives several links away from the starting problem.
rituals.reveal: Worry often feels like one threat while actually containing a chain of increasingly hypothetical events.
rituals.mindBend: You do not have to emotionally prepay every sequel.

rituals.name: SOLVE OR SOOTHE?
rituals.title: SOLVE OR SOOTHE?
rituals.targetPattern: Thinking used either to solve or to regulate emotion
rituals.target_pattern: Thinking used either to solve or to regulate emotion
rituals.precise_subpattern: Thinking used either to solve or to regulate emotion
rituals.vibeLine: Busy-looking thought. Suspiciously little output.
rituals.hook: This loop has a job.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the loop is producing a decision—or trying to make an uncomfortable feeling disappear.
rituals.play: Ask one question: “If I had the perfect answer right now, what would I do differently in the next hour?” If the answer is “nothing,” mark the loop SOOTHE, not SOLVE.
rituals.catch: Check if the thinking is actually linked to action.
rituals.reveal: Problem solving changes a next step. Rumination often changes only the feeling of unfinishedness.
rituals.mindBend: Not every thought that feels like work is doing problem-solving work.
rituals.ritualCard:

rituals.name: WORD-BY-WORD VANISH
rituals.title: WORD-BY-WORD VANISH
rituals.targetPattern: A sentence retaining force through intact wording
rituals.target_pattern: A sentence retaining force through intact wording
rituals.precise_subpattern: A sentence retaining force through intact wording
rituals.vibeLine: Big scary thought reduced to one lonely word.
rituals.hook: We’re going to remove the thought without arguing with it.
rituals.predict: Guess which word feels hardest to delete.
rituals.play: Say the looping sentence. Repeat it, removing 1 word each time from the end until only the first word remains. Say nothing.
rituals.catch: Notice which part of the sentence carried the emotional charge and when the meaning collapsed.
rituals.reveal: Thoughts feel whole, but their impact depends on a sequence of ordinary words.
rituals.mindBend: A sentence can feel enormous until you watch it disappear one word at a time.

rituals.name: IF THE ANSWER ARRIVED
rituals.title: IF THE ANSWER ARRIVED
rituals.targetPattern: Belief closure is required before action
rituals.target_pattern: Belief closure is required before action
rituals.precise_subpattern: Belief closure is required before action
rituals.vibeLine: Turns out certainty may not own the key after all.
rituals.hook: Suppose the perfect answer arrived by courier.
rituals.predict: Guess the first concrete thing you would do differently if the loop were magically resolved.
rituals.play: Imagine an envelope contains the exact answer you want. Don’t open it. Instead name the first action you would take after reading it.
rituals.catch: Ask whether any safe part of that action is available before the answer arrives.
rituals.reveal: Sometimes we wait for certainty before doing something that never required certainty.
rituals.mindBend: Closure can feel like a prerequisite even when the next step is already visible.

rituals.vibeLine: Your loop was running a subscription model.
rituals.hook: Your loop keeps minting questions faster than answers.
rituals.predict: Guess how many new questions appear after you answer the current one.
rituals.play: Write the top question. Allow exactly one follow-up question. Any third question goes onto a parking list without answering.
rituals.catch: Check if the loop’s power comes from question production rather than answer quality.
rituals.reveal: A mind can keep uncertainty alive by generating fresh questions indefinitely.
rituals.mindBend: You do not need unlimited questions to prove you are thinking carefully.

rituals.name: SHUFFLE THREE SCENES
rituals.title: SHUFFLE THREE SCENES
rituals.targetPattern: A memory feels inevitable because events are replayed in one fixed sequence
rituals.target_pattern: A memory feels inevitable because events are replayed in one fixed sequence
rituals.precise_subpattern: A memory feels inevitable because events are replayed in one fixed sequence
rituals.vibeLine: Same scenes, less destiny.
rituals.hook: Same memory. Different edit order.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the meaning changes if three moments are replayed out of sequence.
rituals.play: Pick three snapshots from the event: before, peak, after. Replay them in the order after → before → peak.
rituals.catch: Notice how inevitability weakens when chronology is scrambled.
rituals.reveal: Narrative order helps create a sense that one thing naturally led to another.
rituals.mindBend: A fixed sequence can feel like fate simply because it is the version you keep replaying.

rituals.title: OUTSIDE DATA REQUIRED
rituals.targetPattern: Mind checking for an answer that cannot appear internally
rituals.target_pattern: Mind checking for an answer that cannot appear internally
rituals.precise_subpattern: Mind checking for an answer that cannot appear internally
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain was refreshing a page it does not host.
rituals.hook: This question may need data your brain does not possess.
rituals.predict: Guess whether more thinking can actually generate the missing information.
rituals.play: Name the unknown. Ask: “Would the answer require another person, future event, document, measurement or observation?” If yes, label OUTSIDE DATA.
rituals.catch: Notice the absurdity of searching inside your head for data stored elsewhere.
rituals.reveal: Thinking cannot retrieve information that has not entered the system.
rituals.mindBend: Some uncertainty is not a puzzle. It is a waiting room.

rituals.name: DRAW THE PROBLEM BADLY
rituals.title: DRAW THE PROBLEM BADLY
rituals.targetPattern: A looping issue represented only as words
rituals.target_pattern: A looping issue represented only as words
rituals.precise_subpattern: A looping issue represented only as words
rituals.vibeLine: Ugly diagram, surprisingly less tangled problem.
rituals.hook: Words keep circling.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the loop changes when converted into shapes and arrows.
rituals.play: Draw the problem using only circles, boxes and arrows for 20 sec. No sentences allowed.
rituals.catch: Notice which parts become simpler, missing or newly connected.
rituals.reveal: Changing representation changes what relationships are easy to see.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can feel stuck partly because it keeps arriving in the same format.

unfiltered.play: Identify one non-essential cue and move it out of immediate view—archive, close, file, or hide it. Don’t delete anything important.
unfiltered.catch: Check if mental recurrence changes when the cue stops reappearing visually.
unfiltered.reveal: External cues can reactivate a thought long after the original event.
unfiltered.mindBend: Sometimes unstick means changing what keeps knocking on the door.
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Keep this pass brief and single-pass. Stop if repeating it makes the thought louder, more detailed or harder to leave. Leave room for new evidence after the exercise instead of treating the result as final.
unfiltered.targetPattern: Digital notes/history repeatedly re-triggering a loop
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Remove one nonessential recurring external cue that reactivates rumination while preserving the underlying information.

rituals.name: GOOD-ENOUGH SENTENCE
rituals.title: GOOD-ENOUGH SENTENCE
rituals.targetPattern: Loop sustained by debating exact wording of an unknowable event
rituals.target_pattern: Loop sustained by debating exact wording of an unknowable event
rituals.precise_subpattern: Loop sustained by debating exact wording of an unknowable event
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain wanted copy-editing rights over uncertainty.
rituals.hook: Your mind keeps editing a sentence reality cannot proofread.
rituals.predict: Guess whether finding the perfect wording would change any fact.
rituals.play: Write one deliberately approximate sentence using “something like,” “roughly,” or “I may never know exactly.” Stop editing after one version.
rituals.catch: Notice the urge to perfect language beyond available evidence.
rituals.reveal: Precision can become a substitute for certainty.
rituals.mindBend: You do not need perfect wording for an imperfectly knowable event.

unfiltered.play: Write one deliberately approximate sentence using “something like,” “roughly,” or “I may never know exactly.” Stop editing after one version.
unfiltered.catch: Notice the urge to perfect language beyond available evidence.
unfiltered.reveal: Precision can become a substitute for certainty.
unfiltered.mindBend: You do not need perfect wording for an imperfectly knowable event.
unfiltered.safety:
PAUSE
Keep the written version to one planned pass. Do not keep adding evidence until you feel perfectly certain; uncertainty is allowed to remain. If the same pattern returns later, re-check the new context rather than copying today's answer.
unfiltered.targetPattern: Loop sustained by debating exact wording of an unknowable event
unfiltered.theoryBackbone: Intolerance of uncertainty; perfectionism; semantic processing
unfiltered.mechanismFingerprint: Impose an intentionally approximate wording rule on an unknowable event to block precision-seeking as covert certainty-seeking.

rituals.name: CEILING CAMERA REPLAY
rituals.title: CEILING CAMERA REPLAY
rituals.targetPattern: Loop narrated from one fixed vantage point
rituals.target_pattern: Loop narrated from one fixed vantage point
rituals.precise_subpattern: Loop narrated from one fixed vantage point
rituals.vibeLine: Your ego lost close-up privileges.
rituals.hook: Move the camera where nobody’s ego can hold it.
rituals.predict: Guess what becomes less important from the ceiling.
rituals.play: Replay 10 sec of the scene from a silent ceiling camera. No inner thoughts, motives or close-ups—only bodies, movement and words.
rituals.catch: Notice which pieces of the loop disappear without first-person access.
rituals.reveal: Perspective determines which information feels central.
rituals.mindBend: A scene can stay real while becoming less personal from another camera.

rituals.name: STOP ON A DIFFERENT WORD
rituals.title: STOP ON A DIFFERENT WORD
rituals.targetPattern: Loop continuing because the last repetition cues the next
rituals.target_pattern: Loop continuing because the last repetition cues the next
rituals.precise_subpattern: Loop continuing because the last repetition cues the next
rituals.vibeLine: Your loop tripped over a spoon.
rituals.hook: We’re changing the exit ramp.
rituals.predict: Guess which final word usually launches the next repeat.
rituals.play: Say the loop once, but deliberately replace the last word with a neutral unrelated word like “window” or “spoon.” Then stop.
rituals.catch: Notice the tiny disruption in automatic continuation.
rituals.reveal: Sequences rely on expected endings to cue what comes next.
rituals.mindBend: A ridiculous ending can expose how mechanical a serious loop has become.

rituals.vibeLine: The tenth check may be manufacturing the eleventh doubt.
rituals.hook: You keep reopening the file to make sure it is still there.
rituals.predict: Guess whether another mental replay will make you more certain for long—or less.

rituals.catch: Check if certainty actually stabilised or whether new doubt appeared.
rituals.reveal: Repeated checking can create more opportunities to notice uncertainty.
rituals.mindBend: A file can feel less trustworthy the more anxiously you keep reopening it.

rituals.vibeLine: The sentence wanted dignity. It got a lamppost.

rituals.reveal: Language has continuation pressure independent of the truth of what it is saying.
rituals.mindBend: A sentence wanting an ending is not evidence the ending matters.

rituals.name: MOVE THE TRIGGER OBJECT
rituals.title: MOVE THE TRIGGER OBJECT
rituals.targetPattern: A physical object repeatedly triggering the same thought
rituals.target_pattern: A physical object repeatedly triggering the same thought
rituals.precise_subpattern: A physical object repeatedly triggering the same thought
rituals.vibeLine: Apparently the chair was part of the thought.
rituals.hook: That object may be acting like a doorbell for the loop.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the thought appears automatically when you see or touch it.
rituals.play: Identify one harmless cue—chat thread, notebook, chair, photo, item on desk. Move it out of sight or change its position for a short period.
rituals.catch: Check if the thought frequency shifts when the cue changes.
rituals.reveal: Thoughts are often cued by environments, not only by intention.
rituals.mindBend: A loop can have furniture.

rituals.vibeLine: Midnight brain has lost executive privileges.

rituals.reveal: Cognitive fatigue can increase repetition while reducing flexibility.
rituals.mindBend: More thinking at the wrong time is not automatically better thinking.

rituals.ritual_name: NOT EVERY THOUGHT IS ASSIGNED WORK
rituals.displayName: NOT EVERY THOUGHT IS ASSIGNED WORK

rituals.target_pattern: Thoughts treated as tasks that must be completed
rituals.precise_subpattern: Thoughts treated as tasks that must be completed
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain sent a task request. You are allowed to ignore it.
rituals.hook: A thought showed up.
rituals.predict: Guess what action the thought is implicitly demanding: solve, check, confess, decide, replay, explain.
rituals.play: Name the demanded job. Ask: “Who assigned this, and what happens if I Don’t accept it for ten minutes?”
rituals.catch: Notice the gap between mental appearance and behavioural obligation.
rituals.reveal: Thoughts can generate task-like pressure without external requirements.
rituals.mindBend: A mental notification is not automatically a work order.

VIBE: UNFILTERED

A damn thought showing up does not mean you damn invited it.

HOOK
If thoughts are fully controlled, you should be able to order the next one.

PREDICT
Guess your exact next spontaneous thought before it appears.

PLAY
Pause for 10 sec and wait. Don’t manufacture the prediction on purpose. When a thought arrives, compare it with what you predicted.

CATCH
Catch how the next thought often appears before you selected it.

REVEAL
Thought generation is only partly under deliberate control.

MIND BEND
A thought arriving is not the same as you choosing it.

MOVE ON
↻ NEXT THOUGHT LOTTERY

rituals.name: NOTICE THE ARRIVAL
rituals.title: NOTICE THE ARRIVAL
rituals.targetPattern: Mental events experienced as content rather than arrivals
rituals.target_pattern: Mental events experienced as content rather than arrivals
rituals.precise_subpattern: Mental events experienced as content rather than arrivals
rituals.vibeLine: The thought knocked. You do not owe it tea.
rituals.hook: For once, ignore what the thought says and catch the moment it enters.
rituals.predict: Guess how long until the next clear thought appears.
rituals.play: Wait quietly. The instant any thought arrives, label only 'arrival'—not its meaning.
rituals.catch: Notice the tiny separation between a mental event appearing and you engaging with it.
rituals.reveal: Awareness can notice the event before following the story.
rituals.mindBend: The doorbell ringing does not require opening the door.
rituals.ritualCard:

The voice in your head changes category when it comes out of a speaker.
cheeky.ritualCard:
The voice in your head changes category when it comes out of a speaker.
Record one ten-second voice memo saying the loop exactly once. Play it back once as if it came from a stranger. Stop.
Guess whether your loop sounds wiser, harsher, stranger, or more ordinary when recorded.
Notice what changes when the thought becomes an external sound object. Self-generated inner speech feels fused because it is experienced from inside production.
↻ VOICE MEMO FROM SOMEONE ELSE

MIND BEND
A thought can sound different when it has to survive outside your skull.

rituals.targetPattern: Verbal loops changing when forced into nonverbal structure
rituals.target_pattern: Verbal loops changing when forced into nonverbal structure
rituals.precise_subpattern: Verbal loops changing when forced into nonverbal structure
rituals.vibeLine: The problem had to survive as boxes and arrows.
rituals.hook: Your loop has used words for hours.
rituals.predict: Guess what shape the problem becomes when sentences are unavailable.
rituals.play: Draw the issue using only arrows, boxes, distances, sizes, lines, or stick figures. No labels.
rituals.catch: Notice what disappears because it cannot be drawn—and what structure becomes clearer.
rituals.reveal: Different representations make different information easy to process.
rituals.mindBend: A problem can change when you change the language it is allowed to use.

rituals.name: SLOW-MOTION LANGUAGE
rituals.title: SLOW-MOTION LANGUAGE
rituals.targetPattern: Fast internal speech increasing urgency
rituals.target_pattern: Fast internal speech increasing urgency
rituals.precise_subpattern: Fast internal speech increasing urgency
rituals.vibeLine: Breaking news now delivered by a very slow announcer.
rituals.hook: Your thought is sprinting.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the meaning feels equally urgent when each word gets its own step or finger tap.
rituals.play: Say the looping sentence with 1 word per slow step, finger tap, or beat. No speeding up to fit the thought.
rituals.catch: Check if the sentence keeps the same emotional momentum.
rituals.reveal: Speech rate contributes to perceived urgency and arousal.
rituals.mindBend: Fast language can make a thought feel like a fast emergency.

rituals.name: PUT SPACE BETWEEN THE WORDS
rituals.title: PUT SPACE BETWEEN THE WORDS
rituals.targetPattern: Closely packed words integrating faster than separated ones
rituals.target_pattern: Closely packed words integrating faster than separated ones
rituals.precise_subpattern: Closely packed words integrating faster than separated ones
rituals.vibeLine: The sentence broke into employees instead of one corporation.
rituals.hook: Your sentence is one block because the words are standing shoulder to shoulder.
rituals.predict: Guess whether it feels different when every word gets ridiculous personal space.
rituals.play: Write the sentence with large gaps between every word, or imagine each word on a separate card across a table.
rituals.catch: Check if the thought becomes a collection of pieces instead of one object.
rituals.reveal: Spatial grouping influences how information is perceived as a whole.
rituals.mindBend: A sentence can feel solid because its pieces arrive already glued together.

rituals.targetPattern: Writing and erasing creating a concrete end point for repetition

rituals.precise_subpattern: Writing and erasing creating a concrete end point for repetition
rituals.vibeLine: The thought got one performance and the stage went dark.
rituals.hook: Your loop gets one physical appearance, not infinite reruns.
rituals.predict: Guess whether deleting the sentence feels different from merely deciding to stop thinking it.
rituals.play: Write the loop once on scrap paper or a temporary note. Read it once. Delete, erase, or cross it out in one motion. No rewriting.
rituals.catch: Notice the body-level sense of ending created by a visible transition.
rituals.reveal: Physical actions can provide completion cues that purely mental stopping lacks.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes the mind needs an ending it can see.

rituals.name: BAN YOUR FAVOURITE METHOD
rituals.title: BAN YOUR FAVOURITE METHOD
rituals.targetPattern: A familiar solution blocking a better different solution
rituals.target_pattern: A familiar solution blocking a better different solution
rituals.precise_subpattern: A familiar solution blocking a better different solution
rituals.vibeLine: The nail may not even be a nail.
rituals.hook: Your best-known solution may be hogging the doorway.
rituals.predict: Guess what you would try if your usual method were temporarily illegal.
rituals.play: Take a stuck problem. Ban your first solution strategy for five minutes. Generate three alternatives, including one deliberately strange one.
rituals.catch: Check if the mental field widens once the dominant method is removed.
rituals.reveal: Repeated success with one approach can create mental set.
rituals.mindBend: A familiar tool can become a blindfold when every problem starts looking like its job.

rituals.target_pattern: Active searching sometimes blocking retrieval of a known word
rituals.precise_subpattern: Active searching sometimes blocking retrieval of a known word
rituals.vibeLine: Memory loves appearing five seconds after the search party leaves.
rituals.hook: The harder you chase the missing word, the more it hides behind the furniture.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the word is more likely to appear after thirty seconds of not searching.
rituals.play: When a harmless name or word is stuck, note its first letter or category if known. Switch attention completely for 30 sec.
rituals.catch: Return once and see whether retrieval changed.
rituals.reveal: Fixated retrieval attempts can keep activating the wrong competitors.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes memory needs less chasing, not more effort.

The harder you chase the missing word, the more it hides behind the furniture.

rituals.name: STOP CRAMMING THE THOUGHT
rituals.title: STOP CRAMMING THE THOUGHT
rituals.targetPattern: Repeated review in one burst feeling productive but producing weaker later memory
rituals.target_pattern: Repeated review in one burst feeling productive but producing weaker later memory
rituals.precise_subpattern: Repeated review in one burst feeling productive but producing weaker later memory
rituals.vibeLine: Ten rereads now may just make the page feel familiar.
rituals.hook: Repetition right now can feel like learning even when spacing would teach better.
rituals.predict: Guess what you remember better tomorrow: something repeated ten times now or revisited across several gaps.
rituals.play: Take one useful insight you keep rereading. Read it once now. Schedule the next look later instead of immediately repeating it.
rituals.catch: Notice the urge to reread for fluency rather than future memory.
rituals.reveal: Spaced retrieval usually builds more durable memory than massed repetition.
rituals.mindBend: Feeling familiar now is not the same as remembering later.

Stop cramming the damn insight and let the damn memory actually learn it.

HOOK
Repetition right now can feel like learning even when spacing would teach better.

PREDICT
Guess what you remember better tomorrow: something repeated ten times now or revisited across several gaps.

PLAY
Take one useful insight you keep rereading. Read it once now. Schedule the next look later instead of immediately repeating it.

CATCH
Notice the urge to reread for fluency rather than future memory.

REVEAL
Spaced retrieval usually builds more durable memory than massed repetition.

MIND BEND
Feeling familiar now is not the same as remembering later.

MOVE ON
↻ STOP CRAMMING THE THOUGHT

rituals.title: MEMORY IS A RE-SAVE
rituals.targetPattern: Each recall subtly rebuilding rather than replaying memory
rituals.target_pattern: Each recall subtly rebuilding rather than replaying memory
rituals.precise_subpattern: Each recall subtly rebuilding rather than replaying memory
rituals.vibeLine: Playback button was secretly Save As.
rituals.hook: Every time you open the file, your brain may save a slightly updated version.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your memory today is identical to the first recall after the event.
rituals.play: Compare the earliest version you remember telling with the version you tell now. Look for changed emphasis, wording, missing detail, added interpretation.
rituals.catch: Notice the memory's edit history.
rituals.reveal: Recall is reconstructive and can alter later memory.
rituals.mindBend: Remembering is not pressing play on an untouched recording.

rituals.name: STOP DESCRIBING THE FACE
rituals.title: STOP DESCRIBING THE FACE
rituals.targetPattern: Putting an experience into words distorting nonverbal memory
rituals.target_pattern: Putting an experience into words distorting nonverbal memory
rituals.precise_subpattern: Putting an experience into words distorting nonverbal memory
rituals.vibeLine: Words somehow made the face less face-like.
rituals.hook: Sometimes explaining what you saw makes recognition worse.
rituals.predict: Guess whether describing a face in detail helps you recognise it later.
rituals.play: Think of a familiar face. Describe it in words for 20 sec, then imagine the face again. Notice whether the verbal description feels poorer than the visual whole.
rituals.catch: Catch the mismatch between verbal features and holistic recognition.
rituals.reveal: Verbalising some perceptual memories can interfere with their original representation.
rituals.mindBend: Not every memory gets clearer when translated into words.

rituals.vibeLine: You kept checking whether it was gone by reopening it.
rituals.hook: Fighting a memory can turn the session into nothing but memory-monitoring.

rituals.vibeLine: B, D, G just started wearing each other's name badges.

rituals.predict: Guess which is harder: B-D-G-P-T or K-R-M-L-F.

rituals.mindBend: Sometimes forgetting is acoustic traffic, not poor effort.

Old learning left invisible scaffolding.

You may not be able to perform it now, yet your brain can still have invisible leftovers.
jolly.ritualCard:
You may not be able to perform it now, yet your brain can still have invisible leftovers.
Return to one harmless old skill, word set, route, or procedure. Compare how quickly familiarity and performance return versus the original learning period.
Guess how long relearning will take compared with the first time you learned it.
Notice hidden learning reveal itself through speed. Prior learning can survive as savings even when unaided recall or performance is poor.
